opening.headline: I heard that there are additional conditions in areas such as employment, finance, and medical care. What exactly are those conditions and where are they written?
body: Even if the same model and the same API are used, meeting minutes summaries and applicant document ranking have different policy weights. We've heard that high-risk areas come with additional conditions, but not many people have actually seen that in the documentation.

In this lesson, we turn vague rumors into locations in documents. Find out how the policy document uses the word high risk, what human review and notification it requires, and what additional safeguards it requires. At the end, a commentary follows the exercise of determining whether a need has been met with a hiring screening example.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: May account for additional needs for high-risk use
Tasks can be categorized as high risk or not.
Can determine whether additional needs are met

screens.title: They say there are additional conditions attached to employment, finance, and medical care.
screens.lead:
First, compare the two lines of work below. Even though the same model is used, an additional condition is added only to the second line.

Policy base date: 2026-10-23. Distinguish between the version currently in effect and the version scheduled to be implemented. Anthropic has released the 2026-11-12 enforcement version, so you should check again for changes in the enforcement date and high-risk areas and disclosure obligations before actual operation.

visual.alt: An illustration comparing the normal business lines and the high-risk business lines, with locks attached only to the high-risk lines.

paragraphs: Typical tasks include summarizing meeting minutes, translating, and polishing report sentences. High-risk tasks include ranking applicant documents, assisting with loan applications, and responding to medical consultations. Both lines can use the same model and the same API. However, the second line comes with additional conditions that are not in the normal business.

The problem is that in-house adoption is often considered without knowing what the conditions are and where they are written in the document. Conditions known as rumors have no basis, so it is difficult to reflect them in the design or explain them during internal deliberations.

The goal of this lesson is to turn these vague rumors into concrete locations in the document. We look directly at documents from Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic for provisions addressing high-risk uses, and see that their requirements are organized into three prongs: human review, notification, and additional safeguards.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Is the use of AI in high-risk areas itself prohibited, or are there conditions attached to the way it is used? You will be able to answer this question at the end of the lesson.

screens.outro: First, let's think about whether our work involves high risk.

screens.title: Our work touches high risks.
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so think about the task first and then check.

items.prompt: Does our work involve anything that affects people's employment, loans, insurance, medical care or legal status?
items.answer: This may include secondary tasks such as screening or ranking candidates, even if decisions are not made directly. If the person making the decision relies heavily on the results of AI, it is effectively a job that impacts their individual opportunities.

items.prompt: If AI is already being used for that task, who makes the final decision?
items.answer: This question is the core of this lesson. What the policy documents take issue with is not the field itself, but the structure in which AI confirms decisions without human supervision. The starting point for judgment is who the final decision maker is.

items.prompt: Is there a procedure for notifying the parties of the decision?
items.answer: Whether the parties can know that AI was involved is linked to the requirement for notice. If you don't have a procedure in place, think about what needs to be done in light of the notice requirements you'll see in the demonstration.

screens.outro: Now let us find the actual provisions in the policy document.

screens.title: Finding Clause 1: How the document uses the word high risk
screens.lead: Below is a summary of the parts that address high-risk use in the three documents. Select a highlighted passage to see what it means and reading tips.

data.text: Google prohibits the use of Automated decisions that result in significant disadvantages to individuals without human supervision in high-risk areas such as employment, healthcare, finance, law, housing, insurance, and social welfare. OpenAI blocks the use of Automation without human review for high-risk decisions in sensitive domains including employment, finance and credit, education, healthcare, and law enforcement. Anthropic separately categorizes specific high-risk uses for individuals under High-risk Use Case Requirements.

marks.span: Automated decisions that result in significant disadvantages to individuals without human supervision
marks.note: This is the key phrase in Article 1, Article 8 of Google's policy. Keep in mind that it is not the entire high-risk sector that is being banned, but automatic decisions without human oversight.
OpenAI has the same structure. The list of areas is long, but the practice at issue is automation without human review. Adding a human review would get us closer to what this item requires.

Anthropic does not mix high-risk uses into the prohibited list, but places them as a separate bundle of requirements. The name itself shows that it is not a prohibition but a requirement, a condition.

screens.outro: All three papers look at disciplines and unsupervised automated decisions together. It is not a direct ban if only a field is involved, but it becomes a problem when it is an automatic decision without supervision. Next, let's see what the request is specifically.

screens.title: Provision Finder 2: Human Review and Notice
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the two core needs attached to high-risk use. The documents on which each request is based are different.

tabs.label: person review
tabs.body: Google and OpenAI documents have in common language that calls for a structure where decisions are supervised or finalized by humans rather than automated decisions. Additionally, OpenAI prevents licensed legal and medical advice from being provided on a personalized basis without appropriate involvement of licensed professionals. In both cases, the key is that people must actually be able to intervene in the outcome. If it's just a human review in name and you can't make any real changes, it's hard to say that the needs have been met.

tabs.label: notice
tabs.body: Anthropic's guidelines for organizations serving minors require organizations to disclose to users that they are interacting with an AI system. Anthropic policy also prohibits impersonation by making people believe they are talking to a human being. Notification is not only used to notify the fact that it was written by AI, but is also used to allow the person concerned to know whether or not it was verified by a human. It can be considered a notice only if it can be recognized on the screen that the parties see. A single line deep in the terms and conditions does not meet these criteria.

tabs.label: read together
tabs.body: The two demands do not replace each other. Human review is a request regarding the structure of the decision, and notice is a request regarding the parties' right to know. Even if the hiring documents are finalized by a human, the notification requirement remains if the applicant is not informed of the use of AI. Conversely, even if the use of AI is announced, the need for human review is not met if final confirmation is automatic.

screens.outro: We will now check the additional safeguards added depending on the field, in the case of medical and minors.

screens.title: Find Clause 3: Additional Safeguards
screens.lead: As you select an item, the needs in that area will unfold. Check which conditions the document lists in both areas: Medical and Minor.

visual.alt: A side-by-side illustration of additional safeguards in two areas: healthcare and minors.

items.prompt: Healthcare Domain: What Gemini API Doesn't Allow
items.answer: Gemini API additional terms state that they do not permit use in clinical practice or providing medical advice, nor in any manner that requires approval from the medical device regulator. In the medical field, this means that not only is human review required, but the use itself is sometimes limited by terms and conditions.

items.prompt: Minors Area: Age Requirements for Gemini API
items.answer: The Gemini API assumes users are 18 years of age or older and does not allow use of services likely to be accessed by persons under 18 years of age. If the product is intended for minors, you must check these conditions starting with which model to use.

items.prompt: What Anthropic Requires of Organizations Serving Minors
items.answer: Anthropic cites additional technical measures such as age verification systems, content moderation and filtering, monitoring and reporting mechanisms, and safe use information materials for minors. It also requires public documents to disclose compliance with child protection and privacy regulations such as COPPA, and to disclose that they are talking to AI. A high rate of non-compliance may result in your account being suspended or terminated.

items.prompt: What the OpenAI Under-18 Guidelines Require
items.answer: OpenAI cites age-appropriate AI notices, age-appropriate content filters, monitoring and reporting mechanisms including escalation paths for high-risk interactions, and age verification where necessary. It advises not to process personal data of persons under 13 years of age without a no-retention setting, and states that failure to demonstrate compliance may result in a warning or suspension of access.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed that the level of requirements and expressions are different for each document, let's move on to examples. Meeting the conditions of one company does not mean meeting the conditions of another company.

screens.title: Commentary: Conditions for employment screening purposes
screens.lead: We are trying to introduce a system where AI reads thousands of applications and selects the top candidates. The instructor explains the four-step judgment process. Select the next arrow to proceed.

steps.title: Step 1: Determine the field
steps.body: First, determine if the job is in a high-risk area. Employment is listed by both Google and OpenAI documents as a high-risk sector. Therefore, this system should be classified as a high-risk use and not just office automation, and proceed with further steps.

steps.title: Step 2: Determine the crystal structure
steps.body: Here's who confirms the decision: If the AI ​​confirms elimination, it touches directly on the ban as it is an automatic decision without supervision. Conversely, if the AI ​​only sorts the order and a person finalizes the passing target, it is a structure with supervision. Even for the same tool, the judgment varies depending on the crystal structure.

steps.title: Step 3: Check for blocked functions separately
steps.body: OpenAI and Anthropic policies separately block functions that infer emotions or tendencies from faces or voices, or evaluate people based on social behavior. If your recruiting tool includes interview video analysis, make sure this feature is turned on and, if so, excluded.

steps.title: Step 4: Organize the conditions
steps.body: There are four conditions. First, it is finalized by a person. Second, inform applicants of the use of AI. Third, exclude prohibited features. Fourth, we preserve the basis for judgment and records to enable us to respond to objections. Only when these four things are met can a design meet the conditions for high-risk use. Rather than being a requirement written directly into individual clauses of a document, record retention can be understood as an internal operational device for later accounting to ensure that the conditions set forth in the document were actually met.

screens.outro: Now that the conditions are out of the way, let's see how to determine whether the actual design meets them.

screens.title: Explanation: How to determine whether it is satisfied or not
screens.lead: Read the same recruitment design alternately from a perspective that meets only the form and a perspective that meets the substance. Press the toggles to compare how your judgment changes.

states.label: Satisfies format only
states.body: The person in charge approves the AI-generated elimination list all at once by pressing the approval button on the screen. The notice is written in only one line of the terms and conditions of employment. The emotional inference feature is said to be turned off, but there is no record of the setting being confirmed. On the surface, it appears that human review, notification, and safeguards are all in place, but since the decision cannot actually be changed and is not visible to the applicant, it is difficult to say that the needs are met. In this case, the decision will be conditional and re-adjudicated after supplementation.

states.label: Real satisfaction
states.body: The person in charge can look at the AI basis for each candidate and overturn the decision to reject them, and cases of overturning are recorded. The use of AI is written on job postings and application screens. The settings ensure that prohibited features such as emotional inference are turned off, and there is also a path for applicants to appeal. All three requirements are functional and can be judged satisfied. The principle is to leave it conditional if there is even one item left unsatisfied. The difference between the two perspectives is not the presence or absence of a feature, but whether the feature actually works. When making a decision, check whether there are any cases in the record where the person in charge overturned the decision, where the notice text is on the applicant's screen, and whether there is evidence that the ban feature is turned off. If there is no evidence whatsoever, it is not considered satisfied.

screens.outro: Now that we have looked at the judgment method, I will conclude by summarizing the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaway: High-risk use requires human review and notification
screens.lead: We summarize what we have seen so far into three demands and one judgment principle.

paragraphs: High-risk use is judged by looking at the discipline and automatic decision structure together. Even in fields that have a significant impact on individual rights and opportunities, such as employment, finance, and medicine, the use of AI is not immediately banned. What the documents take issue with is automatic decisions without human supervision, and if there is supervision, there is room for it to be opened conditionally.

Additional demands are three-pronged. Human review is only met if it can actually change a decision. The notice must be visible on the screen that parties see that AI is being used. Medical and minor services require additional safeguards such as age verification, content filters, and escalation paths, and some are restricted by terms and conditions.

When determining whether something is met, look at substance, not form. A bulk approval button is not human review, and a single line of terms and conditions is not a notice. If you leave the supporting documents and clause locations in the decision results, you will not have to repeat the same explanations during subsequent inspections and internal deliberations.

In practice, the content of this lesson can be transferred to an introductory review form. The form requires you to write one line at a time about the area the work belongs to, the person making the final decision, how a person can change the decision, the screen informing parties of AI use, any prohibited features turned off, and the location of the supporting clause. This ensures that business and governance staff are speaking on the same basis and reduces the number of items left out of the review process. Once you create a form, you can use it repeatedly whenever a new task is posted.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: The order of high-risk judgment is to check the field, check the decision structure, check separately prohibited functions, and organize conditions.

checks.intro: See for yourself how these three documents address high stakes. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: What do the three policy documents have in common in addressing high-risk uses?
options: The use of AI itself is completely prohibited in the employment, medical, and financial fields.
Together with the field, we look at whether automatic decisions are made without human supervision.
Limit all automated decisions to the same conditions, regardless of field
If only the field is covered, it is considered to be satisfied as long as the notification obligation is complied with.
checks.explain: The documents take issue with automated decisions without human oversight in high-risk areas. Just because it applies to a field does not mean it is immediately banned.

wrong.0: It becomes a problem when it is an automatic decision without supervision, rather than an immediate ban just because it falls into a field.
wrong.2: Because domain conditions are key, not all automated decisions are constrained to the same conditions.
wrong.3: Notice is only one requirement and is viewed in conjunction with other conditions, such as human review.

checks.correctFeedback: That's correct. Discipline and unsupervised automated decisions are together the criteria for judgment.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Look again at the commonalities. The key point is that judgment cannot be made based on just one field.

checks.intro: Match the contents of each clause. Just select the appropriate description for the item on the left from the right.
checks.q: Match the content with the following clauses (documents):
left: Anthropic's Guidelines for Organizations Serving Minors
right: Require users to disclose that they are interacting with AI
Not permitted for use in clinical practice or providing medical advice
Ban automatic, unsupervised, disadvantageous decisions in high-risk areas
Prohibition of customized legal and medical advice without appropriate involvement of experts
checks.explain: Each document imposes different additional conditions, including human review, involvement of a licensed professional, notification, and medical use restrictions.
checks.correctFeedback: All matched correctly. A distinction was made that each document had a different focus of demands.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some pairs were mismatched. Think again about which documents have what kinds of conditions.

checks.intro: Apply the sufficiency judgment seen in the commentary. Just compare and choose one.
checks.q: Will a structure where the person in charge approves the rejection decisions made by AI all at once with the push of a button satisfies the demand for ‘human review’?
options: It satisfies. Because the person pressed the approve button
It satisfies. This is because approval records remain in the system.
does not meet If you add a notice, it will be automatically resolved.
does not meet You must be able to actually reverse the decision
checks.explain: Human review is satisfied when the person responsible can change the decision. Bulk approval is a formality only.

wrong.0: It's not about whether you click, it's about whether you can change your decision.
wrong.1: Having a record does not make the review substantive.
wrong.2: Notice and human review are separate requirements and one cannot replace the other.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. The criterion is whether you have the power to change the decision, not the act of approval.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The problem with this structure is not the presence or absence of buttons. Pay attention to what your reps can do.

glossary.def: It is used in areas that have a significant impact on individual rights or opportunities, such as employment, finance, and medical care.
This is a structure in which AI results are supervised and finalized by humans. Substantial, not formal, intervention is needed.
It is a requirement to let the other party know that they are interacting with AI.
Additional technical and operational measures in high-risk areas such as age verification, content filters, and escalation paths.

misconceptions.myth: If it is a high-risk field, the use of AI is unconditionally prohibited.
misconceptions.fact: What the document takes issue with is automatic decisions without human supervision. Open conditionally if supervised.

misconceptions.myth: As long as the person in charge sees the results, it is a human review.
misconceptions.fact: A substantive review must be able to change the decision. The Bulk Approve button is just a formality.

misconceptions.myth: The notice only needs to be one line of terms and conditions.
misconceptions.fact: It must be legible on the screen the person encounters. It is difficult to view text that is not visible as notice.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: High Risk looks at disciplines and automatic decision structures together.
Human review and notification are basic conditions.
There are additional safeguards for healthcare and minors.
Satisfaction is judged based on substance, not form.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What are the high-risk tasks in our work where AI could impact individual rights or opportunities, and who is making the final decisions now?
